questions.question_english:
McGregor’s ‘Theory X’ posits that:
Employees inherently dislike work and must be coerced or controlled.
options_english: Employees view work as a natural activity comparable to rest or recreational play
Employees are inherently self-directed, highly creative, and actively seek responsibility
Employees inherently dislike work and must be coerced or controlled
Employees are continuously motivated purely by higher-order self-actualization needs
questions.explanation_english: Douglas McGregor’s Theory X is based on autocratic assumptions about employee behavior. It suggests that workers inherently dislike effort, lack ambition, avoid responsibility, and prefer directive supervision. Therefore, management must implement close supervision, rigid controls, explicit rules, and the threat of sanctions to compel employees to achieve organizational goals and complete necessary tasks.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (c) है। मैकगरेगर का 'थ्योरी एक्स' यह मानता है कि कर्मचारी स्वाभाविक रूप से काम से नफरत करते हैं और उन्हें मजबूर या नियंत्रित करना आवश्यक है। यह सिद्धांत यह बताता है कि कर्मचारियों को काम करने के लिए प्रेरित करने के लिए प्रबंधन को कड़े नियंत्रण और निगरानी की आवश्यकता होती है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Employees inherently dislike work and must be coerced or controlled
Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Douglas McGregor’s Theory X is built on autocratic assumptions regarding employee behavior.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following theories of motivation:
    I. Maslow’s Hierarchy of Needs
    II. Vroom’s Expectancy Theory
    III. Herzberg’s Two-Factor Theory
    IV. McGregor’s Theory X and Theory Y
    Which of the following correctly classifies the
    above into Content theories and Process theories
    of motivation?
options_english: Content: I, III, IV; Process: II
Content: I, II; Process: III, IV
Content: II, IV; Process: I, III
Content: I, III; Process: II, IV
questions.explanation_english:
Content theories of motivation, including
     Maslow’s Need Hierarchy, Herzberg’s Two-Factor
     Theory, and McGregor’s Theory X/Y, focus on
     identifying specific internal factors and needs
     that energize human behavior. Process theories,
     such as Vroom’s Expectancy Theory, analyze
     the cognitive mechanisms, calculations, and
     perceptual processes through which motivation
     is initiated, directed, sustained, and evaluated.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (a) है। सामग्री सिद्धांतों में मास्लो की आवश्यकताओं की श्रेणी, हर्ज़बर्ग का दो-कारक सिद्धांत, और मैकग्रेगर का सिद्धांत X/Y शामिल हैं, जो मानव व्यवहार को प्रेरित करने वाले विशिष्ट आंतरिक कारकों और आवश्यकताओं की पहचान पर ध्यान केंद्रित करते हैं। प्रक्रिया सिद्धांत, जैसे कि व्रूम का अपेक्षा सिद्धांत, उन संज्ञानात्मक तंत्रों, गणनाओं और धारणा प्रक्रियाओं का विश्लेषण करते हैं जिनके माध्यम से प्रेरणा शुरू होती है, निर्देशित होती है, बनाए रखी जाती है और मूल्यांकन की जाती है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Content: I, III, IV; Process: II

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Content theories of motivation, including Maslow’s Need Hierarchy, Herzberg’s Two-Factor Theory, and McGregor’s Theory X/Y, focus on identifying specific internal factors and needs that energize human behavior.

questions.question_english: The 'Pygmalion Effect' in leadership and supervision indicates that:
options_english: Unusually low performance expectations from the Principal consistently lead to unexpectedly high academic output from teachers
High expectations and belief in teachers positively boost performance
Instructional supervision is fundamentally defined as a rigorous, systematic inspection aimed at identifying professional faults
Offering direct, merit-based financial rewards and monetary incentives is the single effective way to induce workplace performance
questions.explanation_english: The Pygmalion Effect demonstrates that higher supervisory expectations directly lead to enhanced individual performance. In educational administration, when a Principal holds high expectations, demonstrates genuine belief in teacher capabilities, and provides supportive leadership, teachers internalize these positive expectations, resulting in elevated confidence, improved instructional practices, and heightened professional performance.
